newsitem.title: FRANCE: French doctors' strike widens, new demo planned.
newsitem.headline: French doctors' strike widens, new demo planned.

text.p: A three-week-old strike by French junior hospital doctors against government health spending curbs widened on Wednesday but protest leaders appeared to be looking for a way out.
The strike has now spread to 23 of France's 26 teaching hospitals. Two more joined the action but one voted to go back to work. Another one voted to strike from next Wednesday.
Rank and file junior doctors staged sit-ins on railway lines delaying trains at 10 major cities, including Bordeaux, Lyon, Lille and Montpellier, as part of the protest.

The strikers, charging the government has been deaf to their demands and is not negotiating in good faith, plan to join a protest march in Paris on Thursday by other hospital staff unhappy at cuts in hospital funding.
The protest against government plans to fine doctors if their region overshoots spending limits began on March 11.
It has turned into a test of conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe's efforts to cut France's welfare deficit to qualify for a single European currency in 1999.

Force Ouvriere trade union leader Marc Blondel, who led a public service strike against the government plan in 1995, told France Inter radio: "Little by little, we see that either the Juppe plan will implode or we will move to a different kind of social security with only minimal protection."
But despite tough rhetoric, there were signs that the strike leaders were seeking to limit the damage.
